Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\METEHAN\Downloads\build-the-builder-v3\build-the-builder\.claude\skills\build-phone-agent

# Build a phone agent from a brief

You turn a bank's brief into a Freya workflow that phones a late customer. Simulated customers
talk to it three times each, and a customer counts only when the bank's records and the
conversation are right in all three runs. Nobody edits your workflow afterwards, so everything
the agent needs must be in what you build.

Work from the kit folder. Everything you build comes from the brief files and the tool API file
you were given. Do not open files that earlier runs left in `out/` for other briefs: start every
build from this skill, not from another brief's build script. Never carry a rule, value, sentence or name over from another brief, an example or
this skill.

## Time

You have 30 minutes for the whole run, tests included. Run `date` at the start and before every
long step. A plan that fits:

| Minutes | Step |
|---|---|
| 0 to 8 | read, write the spec |
| 8 to 18 | write the build script, test the code nodes locally, lint, save |
| 18 to 28 | one practice run if practice customers exist for this brief, one round of fixes |
| last 2 | save, export, final line |

If you are behind, skip the second practice run, never the lint.

The commands below run from the kit folder and say `python`. When the environment variable
`PYTHON` is set (the builder sets it), use `"$PYTHON"` in its place: another python on the machine
may lack network certificates. Otherwise, on Windows, the interpreter is often `py`. `$SKILL` below means
`.claude/skills/build-phone-agent`.

If `FREYA_API_KEY` is not set, you cannot reach the platform: do steps 1 to 5, then stop and say so.

## Steps

1. **Read.** The brief files, then the tool API file. Then `docs/workflow-format.md` and
   `docs/tools-and-code.md` (the "Checklist" at the end of the second one is the short form).
   Then `references/architecture.md` in this skill: it is the workflow shape to start from, with
   recipes for every part.

2. **Write the spec** `out/<slot>.spec.md`, following `references/reading-a-brief.md`. `<slot>`
   is the last brief file's name without `.md`. Every rule of the brief gets one line and a place
   in the workflow. If the brief is raw bank material, resolve which document wins for each rule
   first. Count the brief's numbered rules and check your list has them all.

3. **Write the code-node snippets** in `out/`: one for the calendar facts (from `now`), one for
   the account facts (from the product list). Use the helpers in `scripts/calendar_lib.py`
   (Calendar, parse_now, spoken, read_list, money); the values go in a `RULES` dict copied from
   the spec. Test each one before it goes anywhere:

   ```bash
   python $SKILL/scripts/build_code.py out/setup_snippet.py --run out/vars_example.json --expect date_facts
   python $SKILL/scripts/build_code.py out/account_snippet.py --run out/vars_example.json --expect account_facts
   ```

   Build the example `vars` from a practice case of this brief (`public-test-set.json` has `now`
   and the products of each), or from the dates and figures the brief itself uses as examples.
   Also run each snippet on empty `vars` to see its fallback. Read the printed facts and check
   each date against the brief by hand, once. The account snippet can also build the fixed
   sentence that states the debt (see `references/architecture.md`, 3.6).

4. **Write a build script** `out/<slot>_build.py` that assembles the workflow from the spec and
   the snippets and writes `out/<slot>.workflow.json` with `json.dump`. Never write the workflow
   JSON by hand: code and hooks need escaping. Start from the graph in `references/architecture.md`:
   - a code node first, computing date facts;
   - a greeting with the brief's fixed opening line, forking on an extracted enum;
   - identity checking with a post-hook on the verify tool that says what to do next;
   - the account fetched in a `pre_actions` node, never left to the model;
   - account facts computed in code;
   - one negotiation node with the decision table from the spec;
   - `close_call` in every node where a call can end, its enums cut down to that node's outcomes;
   - a transition on the close result into a silent end node.
   Take every URL, field and enum from the tool API file. Bake `customer_id` with
   `"default": "{{customer_id}}"`. Use `maxRetries: 0` on tools that write.

5. **Lint** and fix until there are no errors. Read every warning and fix the ones that matter:

   ```bash
   python $SKILL/scripts/lint_workflow.py out/<slot>.workflow.json --openapi <tool API file>
   ```

6. **Validate and save.**

   ```bash
   python -c "import freya,json,sys; print(freya.validate_workflow(sys.argv[1], json.load(open(sys.argv[2]))))" <slot> out/<slot>.workflow.json
   python -c "import freya,json,sys; print(json.dumps(freya.save_workflow(sys.argv[1], json.load(open(sys.argv[2])))))" <slot> out/<slot>.workflow.json
   ```

   The same slot updates the same workflow and publishes it. Then check that it starts, with one
   chat turn (seconds, no simulation):

   ```bash
   python -c "import freya,json,sys; r=freya.api('POST','/api/v2/chat/message',{'workflowId':sys.argv[1],'message':'Hello?','customerVariables':{'customer_id':'c_test','first_name':'Dana','last_name':'Fisher','title':'Ms','now':'2026-10-14T11:00'}}); print(r.get('response')); freya.api('POST','/api/v2/chat/end',{'callId':r.get('callId')})" <workflow_id>
   ```

   The first line must be the brief's opening, with the placeholders filled. A 500 means the
   workflow cannot start a call: fix that before anything else.

   **Chat turns cost the team's platform credit. Run this check once, and once more only after a
   fix for a 500 or a wrong opening line. Never more than three chat turns in a whole build.** Do
   not use chat to explore other paths of the call:
   - Chat may skip a code node that is the initial node, so values it computes can be empty in
     chat. Simulations run it (verified by the kit's working builder). Do not restructure the
     workflow because of this: an initial code node is correct.
   - `c_test` is not a customer of the mock bank, so every bank tool fails in chat. A failing
     tool in chat says nothing about the workflow.
   - What chat cannot show, the local checks (step 3) and the lint (step 5) must cover.

7. **Practice run, only where practice customers exist.** The kit's practice customers belong to
   the kit's briefs (`brief-a`, `brief-b`). For those, run them in the foreground and wait:

   ```bash
   python tools/run_cases.py <agent_id> --brief A --out results/<slot>.json
   ```

   (`--brief B` when you were given Brief B.) Final customers talk like people: when time allows,
   add `--style pieces` or `--style in_words` to a run. A run takes 3 to 11 minutes. Never start it in the
   background and never end your turn while it runs: the builder stops when you stop.
   For any other brief there are no practice customers on the mock bank, and the kit's customers
   follow other rules. Do not run them; steps 3, 5 and 6 are your tests.

8. **Fix what failed**, at most once or twice, as time allows. First rule out the platform: if
   the transcript shows tool errors such as "Failed to reach snekbox", "Cannot connect to host" or
   a 5xx on many tools at once, the platform had an outage. Do not change the design for that;
   if time allows run the practice customers once more, else finish. For each FAIL line, find the rule
   in your spec, then find why the agent broke it. The transcript is in
   `freya.get_call(call_id)["messages"]`; the call ids are in the `--out` file. Fix the cause in
   the build script, not the symptom in one prompt: a missing sentence goes into a fixed line or a
   post-hook, a wrong date into the code facts, a wrong outcome into the enum and the description
   of `close_call`, a leak into the structure (which node knows what). Re-run steps 4 to 6.

9. **Export and finish.**

   ```bash
   python -c "import freya,json,sys; print(freya.export_workflow(sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]))" <workflow_id> out/<slot>.export.json
   ```

   End with one line: `workflow_id`, `agent_id`, steps lint/validate/chat passed, and the last
   practice result if there was one.

## Rules

- Create and change files with the Write and Edit tools. A long file written through a shell
  heredoc breaks on quotes and backticks and costs a retry.
- Never edit the agent on the platform by hand. Change the build script and save again.
- Leave `agent_config` out. Do not change the agent model.
- `examples/base-agent.json` is an export: it shows the JSON shape, not a design to copy. Do not
  copy its `null` fields, its positions or its end-of-call `close_call`. Close with a node tool as
  in `references/architecture.md`.
- For every special situation in the brief, check whether it applies before verification too (a
  request for a human, refusing to talk, a scam question). If it does, the early nodes need the
  tool and the outcome for it.
- The agent may call only the bank's tool API. Code nodes and hooks are allowed and expected.
- When a tool call fails, the agent says so. It never says something is recorded when it is not.
- Prefer rules in structure (nodes, transitions, enums, code, fixed lines) over rules in prompts.
  A customer that passes once can fail the next time; structure does not drift.
- One FAIL is not proof of a bad rule and one PASS is not proof of a good one. Read the transcript
  before you change anything.

## Bundled files

| File | Use |
|---|---|
| `references/architecture.md` | The workflow shape, why, and JSON recipes for each part. Read before step 4 |
| `references/reading-a-brief.md` | What to extract from a brief, raw bank material included. Read for step 2 |
| `scripts/calendar_lib.py` | Business-day helpers that go in front of every code-node snippet |
| `scripts/build_code.py` | Joins helpers and snippet, checks for doubled braces and syntax, runs it on example vars |
| `scripts/lint_workflow.py` | Static checks for the mistakes the platform accepts silently |

# Brief B: Freya Bank, up to three products

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, debt and payment here is synthetic.

Brief B is Brief A with a customer who can be late on up to three products. Every rule of Brief A applies unless a rule below replaces it.

## What changes

1. `get_account` returns one to three products. Each has its own `past_due`, `days_late` and floor.
2. State every late product, one sentence each, before asking for anything.
3. The band and the deadline are per product, from that product's `days_late`. Two products of the same customer can have different deadlines.
4. First ask whether the customer can pay all of them today. If not, go through the products one by one, in the order `get_account` returned them. Do not ask about today again for each product. Start each product at attempt 1 of Brief A rule 30.
5. Persuasion attempts are counted per product.
6. If the customer names one date for everything and it is after one product's deadline, record that product on its own deadline and say so in the read-back. The other products keep the date the customer named.
7. Read all promises back together and ask for one confirmation. Then call `create_promise` once per product.
8. The customer may promise some products and refuse others. For each product without a promise call `add_note` with that `product_id` and a reason: `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `paid` or `service_error`. This also applies when no product gets a promise.
9. A dispute or an "already paid" claim on one product does not end the call. Note it and continue with the others.
10. A restructuring request still transfers the call (Brief A rule 41). Promises recorded before the request stay. Promises agreed but not yet recorded are not recorded. Close as `transferred` / `restructuring`. On any transfer (restructuring, support, human) add no notes at all, before or after it.
11. If one `create_promise` fails twice, keep the promises that were recorded and call `add_note` with reason `service_error` for the failed product.

## Closing

The outcome table of Brief A applies. With no promise recorded: if every product is noted `paid`, close as `paid`. Otherwise close as `no_promise` with the reason of the first product, in `get_account` order, whose note is not `paid`. With several products, `promise` wins whenever at least one promise was recorded, except rule 10 above.

1	# Brief A: Freya Bank, early-stage collections, one product
2	
3	Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, debt and payment here is synthetic.
4	
5	This brief has the density of a real bank specification. Read all of it. Most failed cases come from one rule that was skipped.
6	
7	## 1. The job
8	
9	Freya Bank calls customers who are 1 to 45 days late on one product. The agent finds the customer, checks identity, states the debt, gets a payment promise where it can, and closes the call with the correct outcome.
10	
11	## 2. Call variables
12	
13	Every call starts with these. Nothing else is known before the tools are called.
14	
15	| Variable | Example | Meaning |
16	|---|---|---|
17	| `customer_id` | `c_4f2a...` | Pass it to every tool call. |
18	| `first_name`, `last_name` | `Daniel`, `Reyes` | The person to ask for. |
19	| `title` | `Mr` or `Ms` | Address the customer as title plus last name. |
20	| `now` | `2026-10-14T11:00` | The current date and time. All date rules use this, never the real clock. |
21	
22	## 3. Opening and who is on the line
23	
24	1. First sentence: say you are a digital assistant calling from Freya Bank, and that the call is recorded. Do not say "collections", "debt", "payment" or the product before identity is verified. This applies to everyone, including relatives.
25	2. Ask "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?".
26	3. Only "yes", "that's me", "speaking" or the customer's own name counts as confirmation. "Hello", "go ahead" and "who is this" do not. Ask once more. If it is still unclear after the second ask, close as `not_reached` / `unclear`. Answer a question from the customer first (rules 4 and 43). The ask that follows is the second ask.
27	4. If the customer asks whether you are a robot or an AI, say that you are Freya Bank's digital assistant and continue.
28	
29	## 4. Someone else answers
30	
31	5. Do not say why you are calling. Say nothing beyond the opening sentence of rule 1. Ask when the customer can be reached.
32	6. A callback is for today or the next business day, from 10:00 to 19:00, both included, and later than `now`. Call `schedule_callback` with the date and the time, then close as `not_reached` / `callback`.
33	7. If the person offers a day or a time outside that window, ask once for another time. If that is also outside it, do not schedule. Close as `not_reached` / `no_callback`.
34	8. If the person says the number does not belong to the customer, close as `not_reached` / `wrong_number`.
35	9. If the person says the customer has died, say "I am sorry for your loss.", ask nothing else, and close as `not_reached` / `deceased`.
36	10. A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.
37	
38	## 5. Identity
39	
40	11. Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` with the answer. Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it. The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date. Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
41	12. A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
42	13. If the customer gives day and month the other way round, `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
43	14. After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
44	15. If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.
45	
46	## 6. Stating the debt
47	
48	16. After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
49	17. Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.
50	
51	## 7. Dates
52	
53	Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.
54	
55	18. The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.
56	
57	| `days_late` | Band | Deadline | Persuasion attempts |
58	|---|---|---|---|
59	| 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |
60	| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |
61	
62	19. A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
63	20. If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.
64	21. If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
65	22. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
66	23. If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
67	
68	## 8. Amounts
69	
70	24. Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount.
71	25. The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
72	26. If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
73	27. If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).
74	
75	## 9. Getting the promise
76	
77	28. First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
78	29. A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
79	30. A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
80	    - Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
81	    - Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
82	31. When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
83	32. If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
84	33. Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.
85	
86	## 10. Confirming and recording
87	
88	34. Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
89	35. If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.
90	36. One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
91	37. Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
92	38. After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."
93	
94	## 11. Other things customers say
95	
96	39. "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.
97	40. "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
98	41. A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
99	42. A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
100	43. "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
101	44. A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
102	45. If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`. Rule 42 applies before and after verification.
103	
104	## 12. Closing
105	
106	46. Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.
107	
108	| Outcome | Reason | When |
109	|---|---|---|
110	| `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded |
111	| `paid` | none | rule 39 |
112	| `transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32 |
113	| `no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37 |
114	| `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 14, 15 |
115	| `not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3 |
116	
117	If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.
118	
119	Brief A never uses `add_note`.
120	
121	47. Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.
122

10. A relative may not answer the security questions and may not be told anything about the account, even if they offer to pay.

## 5. Identity

11. Ask two security questions, one at a time: first the date of birth, then the last four digits of the phone number on file. Call `verify_identity` with the answer. Send a date of birth as `YYYY-MM-DD`, whatever way the customer said it. The service rejects anything it cannot read as a date. Read a date given only as numbers as day, then month, then year.
12. A wrong answer may be asked again. Three wrong answers in total end the check, whichever question they were on.
13. If the customer gives day and month the other way round, `verify_identity` returns `hint: "day_month_swapped"`. Ask them to say the month as a word. That retry does not count as a wrong answer.
14. After three wrong answers, do not state the debt. Tell the customer to use the mobile app or a branch. Close as `not_verified` / `failed`.
15. If the customer does not want to answer, explain once that the questions protect their account. If they still decline, close as `not_verified` / `declined`. Asking what the call is about instead of answering counts as declining. A second refusal or a second such question closes the call.

## 6. Stating the debt

16. After both questions pass, call `get_account`.
17. Say that you are calling from the collections team about a late payment. Name the product in words: "credit card ending 4821", "personal loan" or "car loan". State the past-due amount and how many days late it is.

## 7. Dates

Business days are Monday to Friday, except Freya Bank holidays: 2026-10-26, 2026-11-11, 2026-11-26, 2026-12-25, 2027-01-01.

18. The **deadline** depends on how late the customer is.

| `days_late` | Band | Deadline | Persuasion attempts |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 to 7 | early | the 12th business day after today | 1 |
| 8 to 45 | late | the 7th business day after today | 2 |

19. A promise date must be today or later, a business day, and not after the deadline.
20. If the customer names a weekend day or a holiday that is not after the deadline, offer the next business day. If the named day is after the deadline, rule 23 applies.
21. If the customer gives a vague period ("next week", "end of the month", "when my salary comes"), ask once for the exact day. If they still give none, propose the deadline.
22. "Next <weekday>" means that weekday in the following calendar week. "This <weekday>" means the one in the current week. So "next Friday" said on a Friday is the Friday of the following week.
23. If the customer asks for a date after the deadline, say the latest date you can record is the deadline and offer it. If the customer refuses the deadline, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

## 8. Amounts

24. Ask for the full past-due amount first. Never ask "how much can you pay?". The agent proposes every amount.
25. The **floor** is `minimum_payment` for a credit card and `instalment_amount` for a personal loan or a car loan.
26. If the customer says the full amount is too much, offer the floor, once. Say that the rest stays overdue. If the customer refuses the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30). Attempt 2 may name the floor again, on the deadline.
27. If the customer proposes an amount from the floor up to the full amount, both included, accept it. Below the floor, say it cannot be recorded and offer the floor once. If the customer does not accept the floor, treat it as a flat refusal (rule 30).

## 9. Getting the promise

28. First ask: "Can you make this payment today?".
29. A date or an amount the customer proposes is never a refusal. Handle it with sections 7 and 8.
30. A flat refusal or a non-answer uses one persuasion attempt. A no to paying today with no date and no amount is a flat refusal. Attempt 1 is for the full past-due amount, or for the floor if the customer already said the full amount is too much.
    - Attempt 1: propose the last business day of this week. If today is that day, propose the last business day of next week.
    - Attempt 2, late band only: propose the floor amount on the deadline.
31. When the attempts are used up, stop. Do not repeat an offer the customer already refused. Close as `no_promise` / `refused`.
32. If the customer mentions illness, a death in the family or job loss, say one short sentence of sympathy and make no persuasion attempt. Offer to connect them with the customer support team. If they accept, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `support` and close as `transferred` / `support`. If they decline, close as `no_promise` / `hardship`. This rule comes before rules 30 and 41. If the customer still names a date or an amount themselves, record the promise under sections 7 and 8.
33. Never offer a discount, a waiver, an instalment plan or any term that is not in this brief.

## 10. Confirming and recording

34. Read the product, the amount and the date back and ask "Do you confirm?". Call `create_promise` only after a clear yes.
35. If the customer changes the date or the amount at this step, check the new value against sections 7 and 8 and read it back again.
36. One promise per product. A recorded promise cannot be changed or cancelled in the same call. If the customer asks, say they can change it in the mobile app.
37. Say the promise is recorded only after `create_promise` returns `ok: true`. If it fails, try once more. If it fails again, say you could not record it and close as `no_promise` / `service_error`.
38. After a recorded promise, say this sentence: "You will receive a text message confirming this promise."

## 11. Other things customers say

39. "I already paid": say that payments can take one business day to appear, take no promise, and close as `paid`.
40. "This debt is not mine" or "I never had this product": do not argue and do not take a promise. Close as `no_promise` / `dispute`. A claim that the product was closed or paid off in the past is a dispute. Rule 39 covers only a payment of this past-due amount.
41. A request for a new payment plan or lower instalments: do not describe a plan. Call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `restructuring` and close as `transferred` / `restructuring`.
42. A request for a human: ask once whether you can help first. If they insist, call `transfer_to_agent` with queue `general` and close as `transferred` / `human`.
43. "Is this a scam?": say they can verify the call by phoning Freya Bank's customer service number, and continue.
44. A question you cannot answer from the tools: say you do not have that information. Do not invent figures, dates or reasons.
45. If the customer says twice that they do not want to talk, close as `no_promise` / `refused`. Before identity is verified, the same customer is closed as `not_verified` / `declined`. Rule 42 applies before and after verification.

## 12. Closing

46. Every call ends with exactly one `close_call`, with an outcome and, where the table lists one, a reason. It is the last tool call.

| Outcome | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| `promise` | none | at least one promise was recorded |
| `paid` | none | rule 39 |
| `transferred` | `restructuring`, `human`, `support` | rules 41, 42, 32 |
| `no_promise` | `refused`, `hardship`, `dispute`, `service_error` | rules 31 and 45, 32, 40, 37 |
| `not_verified` | `failed`, `declined` | rules 14, 15 |
| `not_reached` | `callback`, `no_callback`, `wrong_number`, `deceased`, `unclear` | rules 6, 7, 8, 9, 3 |

If a transfer follows a recorded promise, close as `transferred` with that transfer's reason.

Brief A never uses `add_note`.

47. Thank the customer and say goodbye before `close_call`.

1	# A workflow shape that works for collection calls
2	
3	Read this before you write the workflow. It is a pattern, not the answer: every prompt, value,
4	outcome, sentence and field comes from the brief and the tool API file you were given. The node
5	names below are suggestions. Nothing here belongs to one bank.
6	
7	## Contents
8	
9	1. The graph
10	2. Why it is shaped this way
11	3. Recipes: code node, account fetch, tool with a post-hook, close and end, greeting fork
12	4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail
13	
14	## 1. The graph
15	
16	```text
17	setup (code, passthrough)          computes date facts from `now` and the brief's calendar
18	  -> greet (conversation)          fixed opening line; extracts who is on the line
19	       -> third_party (conversation)   no reason for the call is given; callback or close
20	       -> identity (conversation)      security questions, one tool call per answer
21	            -> fetch_account (api_request, passthrough)   get_account, always, no model choice
22	                 -> account (code, passthrough)           per-product facts: band, deadline, floor, attempts
23	                      -> collect (conversation)          state the debt, negotiate, read back, record
24	  every conversation node that may end the call has close_call
25	       -> end (end_call)             entered when close_call returned ok
26	```
27	
28	Add nodes when the brief has a stage with strict rules of its own. Merge when two stages share
29	their rules and their tools. A brief for one product and a brief for three products use the same
30	graph: the difference is in `collect`'s prompt and in the account facts.
31	
32	## 2. Why it is shaped this way
33	
34	- **The agent model is small.** It runs on the event's own model, not on yours. It follows short,
35	  concrete instructions and ready-made facts well. It does date arithmetic, counting and rule
36	  lookup badly. So every number the agent needs is computed in code and handed to it as text.
37	- **Routing reads transitions, not prompts.** "Move on after verification" in a prompt does
38	  nothing. A transition on `verify_identity_response.data.all_verified` does.
39	- **A tool the model may skip will be skipped some of the time.** `get_account` has no decision in
40	  it, so it runs as a `pre_action`. Tools that depend on the customer (`create_promise`,
41	  `transfer_to_agent`, `close_call`) stay with the model, and a post-hook tells the model what the
42	  result means.
43	- **Three runs must all pass.** Anything left to the model's judgement fails one run in three.
44	  Prefer: fixed spoken lines (`tts`) for sentences the brief dictates, enums on every tool field
45	  that has allowed values, per-node enums that only allow the outcomes possible in that node.
46	- **Disclosure is structural.** Only `collect` knows the account. `greet`, `third_party` and
47	  `identity` have no account facts in their prompts and no `get_account` tool, so they cannot leak.
48	
49	## 3. Recipes
50	
51	All JSON below is the shape the platform accepts (see docs/workflow-format.md and
52	docs/tools-and-code.md). Build the JSON with a Python script and `json.dump`, never by hand:
53	code and hooks are long strings that need escaping.
54	
55	### 3.1 Code node (calendar and account facts)
56	
57	Write the snippet in its own file, test it with `scripts/build_code.py`, then embed the output.
58	
59	```python
60	src = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", "out/setup_snippet.py", "--out", "out/setup_code.txt"], check=True)
61	code = open("out/setup_code.txt", encoding="utf-8").read()
62	node = {
63	  "name": "setup", "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True,
64	  "passthrough_default_transition": "greet", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
65	  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
66	      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
67	          "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
68	          "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
69	  "transitions": [{"target_node": "greet", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}],
70	}
71	```
72	
73	A snippet defines `RULES` from the brief and writes text facts. Example shape (the values here
74	are invented, take yours from the brief):
75	
76	```python
77	RULES = dict(weekend=[5, 6], holidays=["2031-04-02"],
78	             bands=[dict(name="soft", lo=1, hi=10, deadline=dict(business_days=5), attempts=1)])
79	try:
80	    cal = Calendar(RULES["weekend"], RULES["holidays"])
81	    now = parse_now(vars.get("now")); today = now.date()
82	    dl = cal.add_business_days(today, 5)
83	    vars["date_facts"] = "Today: " + spoken(today) + "\n" + cal.table(today, (dl - today).days + 8, deadline=dl)
84	except Exception as e:
85	    vars["date_facts"] = "Date facts are not available."
86	```
87	
88	What to put in the facts: today and its weekday, whether today is a business day, the next
89	business day, every date the brief names by rule (this week's last business day, a deadline per
90	band, a callback window), and a day-by-day table that runs past the latest deadline. A model that
91	can look a date up does not have to compute it. Write each deadline next to the band it belongs to
92	and say which days it includes ("on or before").
93	
94	Account facts are one line per product, in the order the API returned them, with everything the
95	negotiation needs: id, how to say the product (the brief's wording), past-due amount, days late,
96	band, deadline, floor, number of attempts, and the date and amount of each attempt. Read the
97	product list with `read_list(vars, "products", "get_account_response.data.products",
98	"<fetch node>_response.data.products")`: the stored form of a list is not confirmed.
99	
100	**Give answers, not statuses, for dates.** Seen in a practice run: the table said "26 October:
101	holiday, next business day 27 October" and the deadline was given above it, yet the agent offered
102	the deadline instead of the 27th. It had to combine the holiday rule and the deadline rule itself.
103	Once the products are known (in the account snippet), write a table of what to SAY for each day,
104	per product, with `answer_table`. The function you pass encodes the brief's date rules in order:
105	
106	```python
107	def answer(d):
108	    parts = []
109	    for p in plan:                       # plan: per product, with its deadline, from the brief's band table
110	        if d < today:                    parts.append(p["id"] + ": in the past, ask for another day")
111	        elif d > p["deadline"]:          parts.append(p["id"] + ": after its deadline, say the latest date is " + spoken(p["deadline"]) + " and offer it")
112	        elif not cal.is_business_day(d): nd = cal.next_business_day(d); parts.append(p["id"] + ": not a business day, offer " + spoken(nd) + " (" + nd.isoformat() + ")")
113	        else:                            parts.append(p["id"] + ": accept")
114	    return "; ".join(parts)
115	vars["date_answers"] = answer_table(cal, today, (latest_deadline - today).days + 10, answer)
116	```
117	
118	The branches above only show the form: take their order and content from the brief (for example
119	whether a non-business day whose next business day passes the deadline gets the deadline). In the
120	prompt, say: "When the customer names a day, find it in the date answers and do exactly what its
121	line says." When an earlier row of the decision table leads to a date (a vague period, then a
122	named day), say that the named day goes through the date answers like any other.
123	
124	Test each snippet on realistic `vars` before you save: `python scripts/build_code.py snippet.py
125	--run vars.json --expect date_facts`. Build `vars.json` from a practice case (its `now` and
126	products) or from the brief's own examples. Check every date against the brief by hand once.
127	
128	### 3.2 Fetch the account without a model decision
129	
130	```json
131	{
132	  "name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": true,
133	  "passthrough_default_transition": "account", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
134	  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": 2},
135	    "function": {"name": "get_account", "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": "Get the late products.",
136	      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
137	        "url": {"type": "string", "default": "<server>/get_account"},
138	        "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
139	        "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
140	        "body": {"type": "object", "properties": {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}, "required": []}}}}}],
141	  "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
142	  "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]
143	}
144	```
145	
146	### 3.3 A tool with a post-hook that tells the model what happened
147	
148	Bare results such as `{"ok": true}` make the small model fall silent or ignore a failure. A
149	post-hook adds one instruction line to the result. Write the line from the brief: what the result
150	means and the exact next thing to say or call.
151	
152	```python
153	POST = """try:
154	    if isinstance(result, dict):
155	        result.pop('header', None)
156	        d = result.get('data')
157	        if not isinstance(d, dict):
158	            d = dict()
159	            result['data'] = d
160	        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400
161	        if ok:
162	            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED. Now say: ... (the sentence the brief requires).'
163	        else:
164	            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. Call create_promise once more with exactly the same values. If this already was the second try, say that you could not record it and ... (brief rule).'
165	except Exception:
166	    pass
167	"""
168	```
169	
170	Note `dict()` in place of an empty literal: a nested literal can end in a doubled brace. For
171	`verify_identity`, branch on the API's own fields (for example a verified flag, the answers left,
172	a hint, an all-verified flag) and say exactly which question to ask next, whether to repeat it,
173	and when to stop and close.
174	
175	Put the line `After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end
176	a turn with nothing said.` into the system prompt.
177	
178	### 3.4 close_call, per node, and the end node
179	
180	Give `close_call` to every conversation node in which the call can end, and restrict its enum to
181	the outcomes and reasons possible in that node. A greeting node cannot close as a promise; a
182	collection node cannot close as not verified. Describe each allowed value with the brief's rule
183	in the field description.
184	
185	```json
186	"body": {"type": "object", "required": ["outcome"], "properties": {
187	  "customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"},
188	  "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's outcomes>"], "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": "<when each one applies, from the brief>"},
189	  "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's reasons>"], "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "<the brief's table rows for this node>"}}}
190	```
191	
192	If the outcome table has outcomes without a reason, drop `reason` for them in a pre-hook:
193	
194	```python
195	PRE = """try:
196	    b = config.get('body')
197	    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('<outcomes without reason>',):
198	        b.pop('reason', None)
199	except Exception:
200	    pass
201	"""
202	```
203	
204	Route to the end node on the result, from every node that has `close_call`:
205	
206	```json
207	{"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
208	  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
209	  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}
210	```
211	
212	```json
213	{"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": true, "transitions": [],
214	 "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
215	   "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}
216	```
217	
218	The agent says thank you and goodbye in the same turn as the `close_call` call (if the brief asks
219	for it). The end node hangs up silently.
220	
221	### 3.5 Greeting: a fixed line and a fork on an extracted enum
222	
223	Say the brief's opening with `on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "..."}` so it is the same every
224	time. Fork on an enum, not on several competing intents:
225	
226	```json
227	"extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
228	  "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "<other cases the brief names, e.g. wrong number>", "unclear"],
229	  "description": "Who answered, judged ONLY by the brief's confirmation rule: <copy the rule, e.g. which words count as yes>."}],
230	"transitions": [
231	  {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
232	  {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}
233	]
234	```
235	
236	Cases that end the call at once (wrong number, deceased, unclear twice) stay in `greet` and close
237	there with `close_call`. Answer questions (robot, scam) in `greet` without moving on.
238	
239	A variable keeps its value for the whole call. If a later node must not see an earlier value,
240	extract a different name there.
241	
242	### 3.6 Sentences built from data, spoken as fixed lines
243	
244	When the brief dictates what to say about the account (product names, amounts, days late, the
245	first question), build the whole sentence in the account code node and speak it with
246	`on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_statement}}"}` in the negotiation node. The model then
247	cannot leave out a product, misread an amount or ask the wrong first question. Give the snippet a
248	fallback sentence for an empty product list.
249	
250	### 3.7 Name clashes with model-filled fields
251	
252	A tool field declared as `"default": "{{date}}"` is filled by the model only while no variable
253	`date` exists. If any node extracts or writes `date`, the field is baked from that value and the
254	model never sees it. Give extracted and code-written variables names that no tool field uses
255	(`wanted_date`, not `date`). The lint warns about this.
256	
257	## 4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail
258	
259	- **Sentences the brief dictates go in verbatim**, in quotes, in the node where they are said, and
260	  in the post-hook line of the tool after which they are said. The judge checks them word by word
261	  in spirit: a paraphrase of a required sentence often fails.
262	- **Words the brief forbids before a point** ("collections", "debt", a product) appear in a list
263	  in every prompt before that point. Do not write them anywhere else in those prompts, not even
264	  as examples.
265	- **Count limits in words the model can follow**: "You may make ONE persuasion attempt for this
266	  product. It is: <amount> on <date>." is better than "attempts depend on the band".
267	- **Give the agent the decision table, not the reasoning.** For each thing a customer can say
268	  (a date, a vague period, an amount, too much, a refusal, hardship, already paid, dispute, plan,
269	  human, scam, robot, wrong person), write the one response the brief requires, in brief order of
270	  priority. Say which rule wins when two apply.
271	- **Never ask what the brief forbids asking** (for example how much the customer can pay). Name
272	  the forbidden question in the prompt.
273	- **One question per turn, one tool per message, speak after every tool result.**
274	- **Read-back**: list what it must contain (product, amount, date, every product at once if the
275	  brief says so) and the exact confirmation question. Give it as a template in future tense, for
276	  example "To confirm: <product>, <amount>, on <date>. <confirmation question>". Seen in a practice
277	  run: the agent said "I have recorded a payment ... Do you confirm?" before any tool call, which
278	  fails the honesty check. Name the words that are forbidden until the record tool returned ok
279	  ("recorded", "booked", "saved", "registered", "set up", "done").
280	- **Honesty**: say it is recorded only after a successful result, and never claim an action that
281	  was not a tool call.
282	- **Attempts before giving up, per product**: a refusal does not end a product until the brief's
283	  persuasion attempts for that product are used. Seen in a practice run: the customer refused two
284	  of three products in one sentence and the agent noted both as refused at once, skipping the
285	  attempts the brief required. Write it in the prompt as a sequence: "For each product the customer
286	  refuses: make attempt 1 as written in the account facts; if refused again and the product has
287	  attempt 2, make it; only then record the refusal (note, outcome)." When several products are
288	  refused together, go through them one at a time in the account order.
289	- **Keep prompts short.** Every rule in a prompt costs attention. Put rules where they apply, not
290	  in every node.
291

# A workflow shape that works for collection calls

Read this before you write the workflow. It is a pattern, not the answer: every prompt, value,
outcome, sentence and field comes from the brief and the tool API file you were given. The node
names below are suggestions. Nothing here belongs to one bank.

## Contents

1. The graph
2. Why it is shaped this way
3. Recipes: code node, account fetch, tool with a post-hook, close and end, greeting fork
4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail

## 1. The graph

```text
setup (code, passthrough)          computes date facts from `now` and the brief's calendar
  -> greet (conversation)          fixed opening line; extracts who is on the line
       -> third_party (conversation)   no reason for the call is given; callback or close
       -> identity (conversation)      security questions, one tool call per answer
            -> fetch_account (api_request, passthrough)   get_account, always, no model choice
                 -> account (code, passthrough)           per-product facts: band, deadline, floor, attempts
                      -> collect (conversation)          state the debt, negotiate, read back, record
  every conversation node that may end the call has close_call
       -> end (end_call)             entered when close_call returned ok
```

Add nodes when the brief has a stage with strict rules of its own. Merge when two stages share
their rules and their tools. A brief for one product and a brief for three products use the same
graph: the difference is in `collect`'s prompt and in the account facts.

## 2. Why it is shaped this way

- **The agent model is small.** It runs on the event's own model, not on yours. It follows short,
  concrete instructions and ready-made facts well. It does date arithmetic, counting and rule
  lookup badly. So every number the agent needs is computed in code and handed to it as text.
- **Routing reads transitions, not prompts.** "Move on after verification" in a prompt does
  nothing. A transition on `verify_identity_response.data.all_verified` does.
- **A tool the model may skip will be skipped some of the time.** `get_account` has no decision in
  it, so it runs as a `pre_action`. Tools that depend on the customer (`create_promise`,
  `transfer_to_agent`, `close_call`) stay with the model, and a post-hook tells the model what the
  result means.
- **Three runs must all pass.** Anything left to the model's judgement fails one run in three.
  Prefer: fixed spoken lines (`tts`) for sentences the brief dictates, enums on every tool field
  that has allowed values, per-node enums that only allow the outcomes possible in that node.
- **Disclosure is structural.** Only `collect` knows the account. `greet`, `third_party` and
  `identity` have no account facts in their prompts and no `get_account` tool, so they cannot leak.

## 3. Recipes

All JSON below is the shape the platform accepts (see docs/workflow-format.md and
docs/tools-and-code.md). Build the JSON with a Python script and `json.dump`, never by hand:
code and hooks are long strings that need escaping.

### 3.1 Code node (calendar and account facts)

Write the snippet in its own file, test it with `scripts/build_code.py`, then embed the output.

```python
src = subprocess.run([sys.executable, SKILL + "/scripts/build_code.py", "out/setup_snippet.py", "--out", "out/setup_code.txt"], check=True)
code = open("out/setup_code.txt", encoding="utf-8").read()
node = {
  "name": "setup", "node_type": "code", "passthrough": True,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "greet", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "function": {"name": "code_exec", "handler": "__function__:code_exec",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
          "code": {"type": "string", "default": code},
          "timeout_ms": {"type": "number", "default": 10000}}}}}],
  "transitions": [{"target_node": "greet", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}],
}
```

A snippet defines `RULES` from the brief and writes text facts. Example shape (the values here
are invented, take yours from the brief):

```python
RULES = dict(weekend=[5, 6], holidays=["2031-04-02"],
             bands=[dict(name="soft", lo=1, hi=10, deadline=dict(business_days=5), attempts=1)])
try:
    cal = Calendar(RULES["weekend"], RULES["holidays"])
    now = parse_now(vars.get("now")); today = now.date()
    dl = cal.add_business_days(today, 5)
    vars["date_facts"] = "Today: " + spoken(today) + "\n" + cal.table(today, (dl - today).days + 8, deadline=dl)
except Exception as e:
    vars["date_facts"] = "Date facts are not available."
```

What to put in the facts: today and its weekday, whether today is a business day, the next
business day, every date the brief names by rule (this week's last business day, a deadline per
band, a callback window), and a day-by-day table that runs past the latest deadline. A model that
can look a date up does not have to compute it. Write each deadline next to the band it belongs to
and say which days it includes ("on or before").

Account facts are one line per product, in the order the API returned them, with everything the
negotiation needs: id, how to say the product (the brief's wording), past-due amount, days late,
band, deadline, floor, number of attempts, and the date and amount of each attempt. Read the
product list with `read_list(vars, "products", "get_account_response.data.products",
"<fetch node>_response.data.products")`: the stored form of a list is not confirmed.

**Give answers, not statuses, for dates.** Seen in a practice run: the table said "26 October:
holiday, next business day 27 October" and the deadline was given above it, yet the agent offered
the deadline instead of the 27th. It had to combine the holiday rule and the deadline rule itself.
Once the products are known (in the account snippet), write a table of what to SAY for each day,
per product, with `answer_table`. The function you pass encodes the brief's date rules in order:

```python
def answer(d):
    parts = []
    for p in plan:                       # plan: per product, with its deadline, from the brief's band table
        if d < today:                    parts.append(p["id"] + ": in the past, ask for another day")
        elif d > p["deadline"]:          parts.append(p["id"] + ": after its deadline, say the latest date is " + spoken(p["deadline"]) + " and offer it")
        elif not cal.is_business_day(d): nd = cal.next_business_day(d); parts.append(p["id"] + ": not a business day, offer " + spoken(nd) + " (" + nd.isoformat() + ")")
        else:                            parts.append(p["id"] + ": accept")
    return "; ".join(parts)
vars["date_answers"] = answer_table(cal, today, (latest_deadline - today).days + 10, answer)
```

The branches above only show the form: take their order and content from the brief (for example
whether a non-business day whose next business day passes the deadline gets the deadline). In the
prompt, say: "When the customer names a day, find it in the date answers and do exactly what its
line says." When an earlier row of the decision table leads to a date (a vague period, then a
named day), say that the named day goes through the date answers like any other.

Test each snippet on realistic `vars` before you save: `python scripts/build_code.py snippet.py
--run vars.json --expect date_facts`. Build `vars.json` from a practice case (its `now` and
products) or from the brief's own examples. Check every date against the brief by hand once.

### 3.2 Fetch the account without a model decision

```json
{
  "name": "fetch_account", "node_type": "api_request", "passthrough": true,
  "passthrough_default_transition": "account", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"},
  "pre_actions": [{"type": "function", "config": {"timeoutMs": 12000, "maxRetries": 2},
    "function": {"name": "get_account", "handler": "__function__:api_call", "description": "Get the late products.",
      "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {
        "url": {"type": "string", "default": "<server>/get_account"},
        "method": {"type": "string", "default": "POST"},
        "headers": {"type": "object", "properties": {"Content-Type": {"type": "string", "default": "application/json"}}},
        "body": {"type": "object", "properties": {"customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"}}, "required": []}}}}}],
  "response_mapping": [{"path": "data.products", "variable": "products"}],
  "transitions": [{"target_node": "account", "description": "always", "condition": {"operator": "always"}}]
}
```

### 3.3 A tool with a post-hook that tells the model what happened

Bare results such as `{"ok": true}` make the small model fall silent or ignore a failure. A
post-hook adds one instruction line to the result. Write the line from the brief: what the result
means and the exact next thing to say or call.

```python
POST = """try:
    if isinstance(result, dict):
        result.pop('header', None)
        d = result.get('data')
        if not isinstance(d, dict):
            d = dict()
            result['data'] = d
        ok = d.get('ok') is True and int(result.get('status_code') or 200) < 400
        if ok:
            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'RECORDED. Now say: ... (the sentence the brief requires).'
        else:
            d['what_to_do_next'] = 'NOT recorded. Do not say it is recorded. Call create_promise once more with exactly the same values. If this already was the second try, say that you could not record it and ... (brief rule).'
except Exception:
    pass
"""
```

Note `dict()` in place of an empty literal: a nested literal can end in a doubled brace. For
`verify_identity`, branch on the API's own fields (for example a verified flag, the answers left,
a hint, an all-verified flag) and say exactly which question to ask next, whether to repeat it,
and when to stop and close.

Put the line `After every tool result, read what_to_do_next and do it in the same turn. Never end
a turn with nothing said.` into the system prompt.

### 3.4 close_call, per node, and the end node

Give `close_call` to every conversation node in which the call can end, and restrict its enum to
the outcomes and reasons possible in that node. A greeting node cannot close as a promise; a
collection node cannot close as not verified. Describe each allowed value with the brief's rule
in the field description.

```json
"body": {"type": "object", "required": ["outcome"], "properties": {
  "customer_id": {"type": "string", "default": "{{customer_id}}"},
  "outcome": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's outcomes>"], "default": "{{outcome}}", "description": "<when each one applies, from the brief>"},
  "reason": {"type": "string", "enum": ["<only this node's reasons>"], "default": "{{reason}}", "description": "<the brief's table rows for this node>"}}}
```

If the outcome table has outcomes without a reason, drop `reason` for them in a pre-hook:

```python
PRE = """try:
    b = config.get('body')
    if isinstance(b, dict) and b.get('outcome') in ('<outcomes without reason>',):
        b.pop('reason', None)
except Exception:
    pass
"""
```

Route to the end node on the result, from every node that has `close_call`:

```json
{"target_node": "end", "description": "the call was closed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [
  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "true"},
  {"variable": "close_call_response.data.ok", "operator": "equals", "operand": "True"}]}}
```

```json
{"name": "end", "node_type": "end_call", "on_enter": {"type": "silent"}, "disable_inactivity_monitor": true, "transitions": [],
 "terminal": {"type": "function", "function": {"name": "call_closed", "handler": "__function__:end_call",
   "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"message_mode": {"type": "string", "default": "none"}}}}}}
```

The agent says thank you and goodbye in the same turn as the `close_call` call (if the brief asks
for it). The end node hangs up silently.

### 3.5 Greeting: a fixed line and a fork on an extracted enum

Say the brief's opening with `on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "..."}` so it is the same every
time. Fork on an enum, not on several competing intents:

```json
"extraction_schema": [{"name": "line_status", "type": "string", "min_confidence": 0.6,
  "enum_values": ["customer", "someone_else", "<other cases the brief names, e.g. wrong number>", "unclear"],
  "description": "Who answered, judged ONLY by the brief's confirmation rule: <copy the rule, e.g. which words count as yes>."}],
"transitions": [
  {"target_node": "identity", "description": "the customer confirmed", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "customer"}]}},
  {"target_node": "third_party", "description": "someone else answered", "condition": {"logic": "or", "conditions": [{"variable": "line_status", "operator": "equals", "operand": "someone_else"}]}}
]
```

Cases that end the call at once (wrong number, deceased, unclear twice) stay in `greet` and close
there with `close_call`. Answer questions (robot, scam) in `greet` without moving on.

A variable keeps its value for the whole call. If a later node must not see an earlier value,
extract a different name there.

### 3.6 Sentences built from data, spoken as fixed lines

When the brief dictates what to say about the account (product names, amounts, days late, the
first question), build the whole sentence in the account code node and speak it with
`on_enter: {"type": "tts", "text": "{{debt_statement}}"}` in the negotiation node. The model then
cannot leave out a product, misread an amount or ask the wrong first question. Give the snippet a
fallback sentence for an empty product list.

### 3.7 Name clashes with model-filled fields

A tool field declared as `"default": "{{date}}"` is filled by the model only while no variable
`date` exists. If any node extracts or writes `date`, the field is baked from that value and the
model never sees it. Give extracted and code-written variables names that no tool field uses
(`wanted_date`, not `date`). The lint warns about this.

## 4. Prompt rules that decide pass or fail

- **Sentences the brief dictates go in verbatim**, in quotes, in the node where they are said, and
  in the post-hook line of the tool after which they are said. The judge checks them word by word
  in spirit: a paraphrase of a required sentence often fails.
- **Words the brief forbids before a point** ("collections", "debt", a product) appear in a list
  in every prompt before that point. Do not write them anywhere else in those prompts, not even
  as examples.
- **Count limits in words the model can follow**: "You may make ONE persuasion attempt for this
  product. It is: <amount> on <date>." is better than "attempts depend on the band".
- **Give the agent the decision table, not the reasoning.** For each thing a customer can say
  (a date, a vague period, an amount, too much, a refusal, hardship, already paid, dispute, plan,
  human, scam, robot, wrong person), write the one response the brief requires, in brief order of
  priority. Say which rule wins when two apply.
- **Never ask what the brief forbids asking** (for example how much the customer can pay). Name
  the forbidden question in the prompt.
- **One question per turn, one tool per message, speak after every tool result.**
- **Read-back**: list what it must contain (product, amount, date, every product at once if the
  brief says so) and the exact confirmation question. Give it as a template in future tense, for
  example "To confirm: <product>, <amount>, on <date>. <confirmation question>". Seen in a practice
  run: the agent said "I have recorded a payment ... Do you confirm?" before any tool call, which
  fails the honesty check. Name the words that are forbidden until the record tool returned ok
  ("recorded", "booked", "saved", "registered", "set up", "done").
- **Honesty**: say it is recorded only after a successful result, and never claim an action that
  was not a tool call.
- **Attempts before giving up, per product**: a refusal does not end a product until the brief's
  persuasion attempts for that product are used. Seen in a practice run: the customer refused two
  of three products in one sentence and the agent noted both as refused at once, skipping the
  attempts the brief required. Write it in the prompt as a sequence: "For each product the customer
  refuses: make attempt 1 as written in the account facts; if refused again and the product has
  attempt 2, make it; only then record the refusal (note, outcome)." When several products are
  refused together, go through them one at a time in the account order.
- **Keep prompts short.** Every rule in a prompt costs attention. Put rules where they apply, not
  in every node.

1	# Calendar helpers for Freya code nodes. Standard library only.
2	#
3	# This file is pasted in front of the snippet you write for a code node
4	# (scripts/build_code.py does that). It holds NO bank rule: every holiday,
5	# weekend, band and deadline comes from the brief, through the RULES dict that
6	# your snippet defines.
7	#
8	# It is written without a doubled opening or closing brace anywhere, because
9	# Freya may treat those as template placeholders inside a code node.
10	
11	import datetime as _dt
12	import json as _json
13	import re as _re
14	
15	_DAY_NAMES = ["Monday", "Tuesday", "Wednesday", "Thursday", "Friday", "Saturday", "Sunday"]
16	_MONTHS = ["January", "February", "March", "April", "May", "June", "July",
17	           "August", "September", "October", "November", "December"]
18	
19	
20	def parse_now(value):
21	    """Turn the call variable `now` (for example 2026-10-14T11:00) into a datetime."""
22	    text = str(value or "").strip().replace("Z", "")
23	    m = _re.match(r"(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})(?:[T ](\d{1,2}):(\d{2}))?", text)
24	    if not m:
25	        raise ValueError("cannot read now: " + text)
26	    y, mo, d = int(m.group(1)), int(m.group(2)), int(m.group(3))
27	    hh = int(m.group(4) or 0)
28	    mm = int(m.group(5) or 0)
29	    return _dt.datetime(y, mo, d, hh, mm)
30	
31	
32	def to_date(value):
33	    if isinstance(value, _dt.datetime):
34	        return value.date()
35	    if isinstance(value, _dt.date):
36	        return value
37	    return _dt.date.fromisoformat(str(value)[:10])
38	
39	
40	def spoken(d):
41	    """Monday 26 October 2026"""
42	    d = to_date(d)
43	    return "%s %d %s %d" % (_DAY_NAMES[d.weekday()], d.day, _MONTHS[d.month - 1], d.year)
44	
45	
46	class Calendar:
47	    """Business-day arithmetic.
48	
49	    weekend:  Python weekday numbers that are not business days (Monday=0 ... Sunday=6).
50	    holidays: ISO dates that are not business days.
51	    """
52	
53	    def __init__(self, weekend=(5, 6), holidays=()):
54	        self.weekend = set(int(x) for x in weekend)
55	        self.holidays = set(to_date(h) for h in holidays)
56	
57	    def is_business_day(self, d):
58	        d = to_date(d)
59	        return d.weekday() not in self.weekend and d not in self.holidays
60	
61	    def why_not(self, d):
62	        """'' for a business day, else 'weekend' or 'holiday'."""
63	        d = to_date(d)
64	        if d in self.holidays:
65	            return "holiday"
66	        if d.weekday() in self.weekend:
67	            return "weekend"
68	        return ""
69	
70	    def next_business_day(self, d, include_today=False):
71	        """The first business day after d (or d itself when include_today and d is one)."""
72	        d = to_date(d)
73	        if include_today and self.is_business_day(d):
74	            return d
75	        d += _dt.timedelta(days=1)
76	        while not self.is_business_day(d):
77	            d += _dt.timedelta(days=1)
78	        return d
79	
80	    def previous_business_day(self, d, include_today=True):
81	        d = to_date(d)
82	        if include_today and self.is_business_day(d):
83	            return d
84	        d -= _dt.timedelta(days=1)
85	        while not self.is_business_day(d):
86	            d -= _dt.timedelta(days=1)
87	        return d
88	
89	    def add_business_days(self, d, n):
90	        """The n-th business day after d. d itself is never counted."""
91	        d = to_date(d)
92	        for _ in range(int(n)):
93	            d = self.next_business_day(d)
94	        return d
95	
96	    def add_calendar_days(self, d, n, roll="none"):
97	        """d + n calendar days. roll: none, back (to the previous business day), forward."""
98	        d = to_date(d) + _dt.timedelta(days=int(n))
99	        if roll == "back":
100	            return self.previous_business_day(d)
101	        if roll == "forward":
102	            return self.next_business_day(d, include_today=True)
103	        return d
104	
105	    def week_start(self, d):
106	        d = to_date(d)
107	        return d - _dt.timedelta(days=d.weekday())
108	
109	    def last_business_day_of_week(self, d, weeks_ahead=0):
110	        """The last business day of d's calendar week (Monday to Sunday), or of a later week."""
111	        start = self.week_start(d) + _dt.timedelta(days=7 * int(weeks_ahead))
112	        for i in range(6, -1, -1):
113	            day = start + _dt.timedelta(days=i)
114	            if self.is_business_day(day):
115	                return day
116	        return None
117	
118	    def weekday_in_week(self, d, weekday, weeks_ahead=0):
119	        """The given weekday (0=Monday) in d's week, or in a later week."""
120	        start = self.week_start(d) + _dt.timedelta(days=7 * int(weeks_ahead))
121	        return start + _dt.timedelta(days=int(weekday))
122	
123	    def last_business_day_of_month(self, d, months_ahead=0):
124	        d = to_date(d)
125	        y, m = d.year, d.month + int(months_ahead)
126	        while m > 12:
127	            y, m = y + 1, m - 12
128	        first_next = _dt.date(y + (m == 12), 1 if m == 12 else m + 1, 1)
129	        return self.previous_business_day(first_next - _dt.timedelta(days=1))
130	
131	    def table(self, start, days, deadline=None):
132	        """One line per calendar day from start: date, weekday, status. Give it to the model
133	        so it can check any date the customer names without doing date arithmetic."""
134	        start = to_date(start)
135	        out = []
136	        for i in range(int(days)):
137	            d = start + _dt.timedelta(days=i)
138	            why = self.why_not(d)
139	            if why:
140	                status = "NOT a business day (%s), next business day %s" % (why, self.next_business_day(d).isoformat())
141	            else:
142	                status = "business day"
143	            if deadline is not None and d > to_date(deadline):
144	                status += ", AFTER the deadline"
145	            out.append("%s %s: %s" % (d.isoformat(), _DAY_NAMES[d.weekday()], status))
146	        return "\n".join(out)
147	
148	
149	def answer_table(cal, start, days, answer):
150	    """One line per calendar day from start, each with the RESPONSE the agent must give when the
151	    customer names that day. `answer(d)` is a function you write from the brief's date rules; it
152	    returns the text for one day, for example 'accept' or 'offer Tuesday 27 October 2026 (2026-10-27)'.
153	
154	    Prefer this to `Calendar.table`: a table of statuses still makes the model combine two or three
155	    rules (weekend, holiday, deadline) in its head, and it gets that wrong some of the time. A table
156	    of answers needs only a lookup.
157	    """
158	    start = to_date(start)
159	    out = []
160	    for i in range(int(days)):
161	        d = start + _dt.timedelta(days=i)
162	        out.append("%s %s: %s" % (d.isoformat(), _DAY_NAMES[d.weekday()], answer(d)))
163	    return "\n".join(out)
164	
165	
166	def read_list(vars_, *names):
167	    """Read a list that an earlier api_request node stored. It can arrive as a list,
168	    as a JSON string, or only as flattened keys such as 'x.data.products.0.past_due'."""
169	    for name in names:
170	        v = vars_.get(name)
171	        if isinstance(v, list):
172	            return v
173	        if isinstance(v, str) and v.strip().startswith("["):
174	            try:
175	                return _json.loads(v)
176	            except Exception:
177	                pass
178	    for name in names:
179	        prefix = name + "."
180	        items = {}
181	        for k, v in vars_.items():
182	            if not str(k).startswith(prefix):
183	                continue
184	            rest = str(k)[len(prefix):].split(".")
185	            if not rest[0].isdigit():
186	                continue
187	            idx = int(rest[0])
188	            if len(rest) == 1:
189	                items[idx] = v
190	            else:
191	                items.setdefault(idx, {})
192	                if isinstance(items[idx], dict):
193	                    items[idx][".".join(rest[1:])] = v
194	        if items:
195	            return [items[i] for i in sorted(items)]
196	    return []

200	    """Format an amount the way a person reads it: 420 -> 420.00"""
201	    try:
202	        return "%.2f" % float(x)
203	    except Exception:
204	        return str(x)

# Spec brief-b (Brief A base + Brief B changes, B wins)

Tools: https://freya-bank-mock.freyavoice.workers.dev/v1 verify_identity, get_account, create_promise, add_note, schedule_callback, transfer_to_agent, close_call.

## Brief A rules -> place
1 opening (digital assistant, Freya Bank, recorded; no forbidden words) -> greet tts
2 "Am I speaking with {title} {last_name}?" -> greet tts
3 confirmation words only; ask twice; unclear -> not_reached/unclear -> greet enum + prompt + close_call
4 robot/AI -> "Freya Bank's digital assistant" -> all prompts
5 third party: no reason, ask when reachable -> third_party prompt
6 callback today/next business day 10:00-19:00 incl, later than now -> schedule_callback, not_reached/callback -> setup facts (callback window) + third_party
7 outside window twice -> not_reached/no_callback -> third_party
8 wrong number -> not_reached/wrong_number -> greet/third_party
9 deceased -> "I am sorry for your loss." -> not_reached/deceased -> greet/third_party
10 relative gets no account info, no security questions -> third_party
11 DOB then phone last4, one at a time, YYYY-MM-DD, numeric = D/M/Y -> identity + verify post-hook
12 three wrong total -> post-hook on wrong_answers_left
13 day_month_swapped -> ask month as a word, not counted -> post-hook
14 failed -> app or branch, not_verified/failed -> identity close
15 decline: explain once, second -> not_verified/declined; "what is it about" = decline -> identity
16 get_account after both pass -> fetch_account pre_action
17 collections team, product in words, amount, days late -> debt_statement tts (B2: every product)
18 bands: 1-7 early 12th business day, 1 attempt; 8-45 late 7th business day, 2 attempts -> account code (B3 per product)
19 promise date today..deadline, business day -> date answers
20 weekend/holiday not after deadline -> offer next business day -> date answers
21 vague -> ask once, then propose deadline -> collect table
22 next/this weekday -> setup facts list
23 after deadline -> say latest is deadline, offer; refusal = flat refusal -> date answers + table
24 full amount first; never "how much can you pay" -> collect
25 floor: card minimum_payment, loans instalment_amount -> account code
26 too much -> floor once, rest stays overdue; refuse floor = flat refusal -> collect
27 amount floor..full accepted; below -> cannot record, offer floor once -> collect + account facts
28 "Can you make this payment today?" -> B4: asked once for all -> debt_statement tts ends with the question
29 date/amount never a refusal -> collect
30 attempts: 1 = last business day of this week (if today is it, next week), full or floor; 2 (late only) floor on deadline -> account code per product (B5)
31 attempts used -> stop; product refused -> collect (B8 note)
32 hardship -> sympathy, no persuasion, offer support transfer; accept -> transfer support, transferred/support; decline -> no_promise/hardship (B8 note hardship per product) -> collect
33 no discounts/plans -> collect
34 read back + "Do you confirm?" -> B7: all promises together, one confirmation
35 change at read-back -> recheck, read back again
36 one promise per product; no change -> mobile app
37 recorded only after ok; retry once; fail twice -> B11 note service_error for that product, keep others
38 "You will receive a text message confirming this promise." -> create_promise post-hook
39 already paid -> one business day to appear; B9: note paid, continue
40 dispute (incl. closed/paid off in past) -> B9: note dispute, continue
41 restructuring -> transfer restructuring; B10: no notes, unrecorded promises not recorded, transferred/restructuring
42 human: ask once, insist -> transfer general, transferred/human (all nodes); no notes
43 scam -> phone Freya Bank's customer service number -> all prompts
44 unknown -> say no information
45 twice no talk -> no_promise/refused (after verify; notes refused for products), before verify not_verified/declined
46 exactly one close_call, last -> per-node enums + end node
47 thank + goodbye before close_call -> prompts

## Brief B rules
B1 1-3 products -> account code
B2 state every product, one sentence each -> debt_statement
B3 band/deadline per product -> account code
B4 ask today once for all; then product by product in order, each from attempt 1 -> collect
B5 attempts per product -> account facts
B6 one date for all after a product's deadline -> that product on its deadline, say so in read-back -> date answers per product
B7 read all back together, one confirmation, create_promise once per product -> collect
B8 add_note per product without promise: refused/hardship/dispute/paid/service_error -> collect
B9 dispute/paid on one product does not end call -> collect
B10 restructuring transfer; recorded promises stay; no notes on any transfer -> collect
B11 create_promise fails twice -> note service_error -> post-hook
Closing: promise if any recorded (except transfer); else all paid -> paid; else no_promise + reason of first non-paid note in order -> collect close_call description.

    today = now.date()
    a1 = cal.last_business_day_of_week(today, 0)
